groups.content:

Discovery

  • Tollund Man was found by two brothers who were cutting peat to burn as [9]

  • a substance from sphagnum moss tans the [10]

Evidence from the bodies

  • Tollund Man's last meal: porridge made from barley, [11] and wild seeds
  • Lindow Man: his well-kept [12] suggest that he did not do physical work

Possible explanations

  • a sacrifice to the gods at a time of crisis, such as a poor [13]
  • the execution of a criminal

groups.content:
Why fungi deserve more respect

Brennan argues that fungi should be taken more seriously. Only a small proportion of fungal species cause [17], while many others are essential to the health of forests and farms. Most land plants rely on [18] with fungi, which provide water and minerals in return for sugars.

However, fungi are under threat. Modern [19] methods destroy the networks of fungal threads in the soil, and the [20] used to protect crops kill useful fungi as well as harmful ones.

C   curiosity

E   patience

I   confidence

groups.content:
The characteristics of good listening

Hannah Reid and her colleagues have identified four characteristics of good listening. Listeners should give the speaker their complete [31], and should avoid forming [32] before the speaker has finished. They should ask open questions that show [33], and check that they have understood correctly by giving a [34] of what has been said.

Reid also recommends removing distractions. Research suggests that even the [35] of a mobile phone can make conversations feel less close.

groups.instruction:
Questions 36-40

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 3?

In boxes 36-40 on your answer sheet, write

TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
FALSE if the statement contradicts the information
NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this

questions.explanation: Answer: TRUE Hundreds have been found, ' most of them in one relatively small part of north-western Europe '.
Answer: NOT GIVEN The passage gives the number and locations of bog bodies but says nothing about the proportion of men and women.
Answer: TRUE His face looked so fresh that ' they assumed they had found the victim of a recent murder '.
Answer: FALSE ' His date has been more controversial ': some place his death in the first century CE, others earlier.
Answer: TRUE Bogs are cold, acidic and low in oxygen – ' conditions in which the bacteria that normally break down flesh cannot survive '.
Answer: FALSE Acid dissolves calcium, so ' in many bog bodies the bones have become soft or have disappeared almost entirely ', while skin can survive for over 2,000 years.
Answer: TRUE ' his last meal had been a kind of porridge made from barley, flax and the seeds of various wild plants ', eaten 12-24 hours before death.
Answer: NOT GIVEN His nails suggest he 'may have been a person of high status', but nothing is said about royalty.
Answer: fuel 'two brothers who were cutting peat to use as fuel '.
Answer: skin Sphagnum 'releases a substance that reacts with the skin and effectively tans it'.
Answer: flax 'porridge made from barley, flax and the seeds of various wild plants'.
Answer: fingernails 'His fingernails were smooth and neatly trimmed', suggesting he did not do heavy physical work.
Answer: harvest Sacrifices 'at times of crisis such as a failed harvest '.

text.en: They are more common in soil than in water.
They are more dangerous than most people realise.
They appeared on Earth at the same time as humans.
Most people pay little attention to them.

questions.explanation: Answer: D ' most of us notice them only when a mushroom appears on the lawn or mould spreads across a forgotten loaf of bread '. Fungi were here 'long before us' (C).

text.en: fungi are closely related to plants.
scientists have now identified most species of fungi.
a single fungus is the largest living thing known.
fungi can live longer than any tree.

questions.explanation: Answer: C ' What astonishes me most, however, is that the largest known living organism on Earth is not a whale or a tree but a fungus '. Fungi are closer to us than to plants (A); most species remain unknown (B).

text.en: explaining how knowledge about fungi developed over time
comparing different scientists' theories about spores
describing a disagreement between early naturalists
giving details of how fungi cause disease

questions.explanation: Answer: A The paragraph moves from ancient beliefs (thunder), to eighteenth-century microscopes and spores, to Fleming's discovery in 1928 – a history of understanding.
Answer: G (disease) ' Only a small proportion of fungal species cause disease in humans '.
Answer: B (cooperation) ' land plants depend on partnerships with such fungi ', exchanging sugars for water and minerals.
Answer: H (farming) ' Modern farming, with its heavy ploughing and use of artificial fertilisers, destroys the networks of mycelium '.
Answer: E (chemicals) ' the chemicals sprayed on crops to kill harmful fungi also kill beneficial ones '.
Answer: NO Farming with heavy ploughing ' destroys the networks of mycelium in the soil '.
Answer: YES ' there is far less evidence than is often claimed that trees use these connections to help one another '; the writer calls this caution 'refreshing'.
Answer: NOT GIVEN The writer mentions a chapter on a fungal disease threatening banana plantations, but says nothing about its length.
Answer: YES 'not every chapter is for the squeamish', and readers may need to ' overcome their distaste '.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Firms are 'developing leather substitutes made from fungi', but their cost is not mentioned.
Answer: NO Grown houses are only imagined: ' this is still a distant prospect '. Only packaging and insulation exist already.

text.en: Most people remember conversations accurately.
A common belief about listening may be wrong.
Listening skills differ from one culture to another.
There is little research into how people listen.

questions.explanation: Answer: B Most of us think we are good listeners, yet research suggests otherwise, and ' Good listening ... is not a talent that only a lucky few are born with '. People remember 'only a fraction' (A).

text.en: It is similar to having a good memory.
Earlier studies of it used unreliable methods.
The effect of the situation on it was underestimated.
Different branches of research disagree about it.

questions.explanation: Answer: C ' how well someone listens depends far more on the situation they are in than we ever assumed '. The different fields 'all point the same way' (D); the comparison with memory is the old view (A).

text.en: is usually better than they believe.
varies from one situation to another.
depends mainly on their personality.
improves naturally with age.

questions.explanation: Answer: B ' The same person can listen extremely well in one conversation and very poorly in the next. '

text.en: a problem with research into listening
a type of person who tends to listen badly
a disagreement about the effects of technology
a practical way of improving listening

questions.explanation: Answer: D ' one of the most effective ways of listening better, which is to remove distractions ' – especially phones.
Answer: D (attention) ' The first is full attention: not simply being silent ' – silence (B) is not enough.
Answer: A (opinions) ' a willingness to hold back from forming opinions , at least until the speaker has finished'.
Answer: C (curiosity) ' The third is curiosity, expressed through open questions '.
Answer: F (summary) Checking understanding ' by summarising what has been said '.
Answer: G (presence) The phone never rang: ' The mere presence of a phone seems to signal that the listener's attention might be taken away'.
Answer: FALSE ' The researchers randomly assigned the listeners to one of two groups ' – the listeners did not choose.
Answer: NOT GIVEN We are told what the students were asked to do, but not what they were told about the purpose of the study.
Answer: NOT GIVEN An example topic is given, but there is no information about whether different topics produced different results.
Answer: TRUE In the first study speakers were 'more likely to consider different sides of the problem'; in the second, they ' described their own opinions in less extreme terms '.
Answer: TRUE ' research shows only a weak connection between listening quality and either intelligence or personality '.
